central_question: How were capitulum traits differentiated through evolutionary time, and when trait-changing lineages can be bounded in calendar time, did particular environmental states, changes or instabilities repeatedly accompany that differentiation?

chapter1.estimand_direction: present phenotype ~ present environmental gradient after explicit spatial controls
chapter1.not_inferred: the environment that originally generated the trait difference

chapter2.estimand_direction: trait-transition opportunity through evolutionary time ~ historical environmental level/change/variability
chapter2.not_inferred: natural selection or adaptation from historical alignment alone

thesis_symmetry.later_integration: Only after both chapters are independently frozen, compare whether historical differentiation direction is retained, lost, reversed or replaced in present maintenance. This comparison is a thesis synthesis layer, not a Chapter 2 row-selection rule.
thesis_symmetry.chapter3: Test candidate environment -> trait function -> reproductive fitness in ancestry-resolved material before using an adaptive explanation.

chapter2_evidence_order: trait recurrence: minimum number of changes under admitted histories
relative temporal depth: internal versus terminal placement and relative lineage-depth envelopes
calendar identifiability: which transition-bearing branches can independently be bounded by published chronology
paleogeographic identifiability: alternative ancestral-area/location scenarios rather than modern-tip substitution
historical environmental level, signed change, absolute change and temporal variability within dated event windows
matched same-duration background windows in the same paleolocation scenario
same-direction recurrence across at least two independently bounded homologous transitions
public-data identifiability ceiling and Chapter 3 mechanism/fitness handoff

orientation.history_status: 4-6 minimum changes; relative depth spans internal-to-terminal placements
orientation.dated_event_status: one core-Nipponocirsium transition envelope has chronology x paleolocation support
orientation.historical_environment_status: evaluable for PALEO-PGEM BIO1/BIO4/BIO12/BIO15 branch-window diagnostics

phyllary_posture.history_status: 3 minimum changes; relatively deep placements remain admissible
phyllary_posture.dated_event_status: published dated sister phenotype contrasts exist but are not reconstructed posture transitions

stickiness.dated_event_status: published range-event ages exist for some taxa but are not trait-transition ages

flower_colour.history_status: two conditional white-lineage terminal branch envelopes provide natural differentiation cases; a global fixed-state transition history is not resolved
flower_colour.dated_event_status: conditional Taiwan and Arenicola terminal branch envelopes
flower_colour.historical_environment_status: general climate context may be explored only with explicit branch/paleolocation uncertainty; a historical radiative driver remains not_evaluable without a commensurate radiation series

allowed: environmental regime associated with a bounded differentiation window
environmental_trigger_language.requires_repeated_events: A common/repeated trigger candidate requires at least two independently bounded homologous transition events with compatible direction.

role_of_space_breadth_pilot.use: Describe whether present trait states are geographically broad or localized and expose coverage limitations; it may help interpret lineage opportunities but is not the primary Chapter 2 biological question.

role_of_current_trait_environment_screen.use: Generate possible mechanistic or historical variables to audit, provided the historical variable is independently available.
role_of_current_trait_environment_screen.selection_rule: No present-day association can retroactively define which historical event/environment rows are considered primary.

claim_boundary: Minimum changes are lower bounds and do not identify independent origins.
Relative lineage depth is topology-based and is not calendar time.
A published lineage split or dispersal date is not an exact trait-transition age.
Paleolocation boxes are alternative scenarios, not ancestral-area probabilities.
Event-window environmental alignment does not establish the transition instant, exposure of the actual ancestral population, natural selection or adaptation.
A single dated event cannot establish a repeated environmental trigger.
Current maintenance and historical differentiation are kept independent until the later thesis-synthesis step.
